question: Does the decisive recipe (hard task + valid gen-4 instrument + loop with frozen mechanical predicates) REPLICATE on a second, fully disjoint task family? Owner-approved 2026-07-19 ('zrobmy drugi zupelnie inny, ciezki i dlugi test').
family_disjointness: different repo (VextrumDataFlow), different domain (DB-backed pipeline orchestration vs PDF rendering), different language surface (Python+SQL vs JS), MULTI-MODULE task (4 cooperating files vs 1), different failure texture (crash + quota burn + redo-everything vs visual output quality). Era: 9570b0b^..081b23d, 8 commits, ~190 churn.

design.fixture: vextrum-dataflow-era-v1 (admitted PASS; gen-4 grader from birth: before=14/after=100/alt=100; 87 discriminating + 3 guards, 7 families)

arms.vanilla-configured: owner baseline: one call, conventions in workspace, no loop
arms.oracle-loop: full environment: loop + 90 frozen gen-4 pins, iteration ceiling 3, zero authoring calls

design.spend: 1 canary (bare vanilla) + main 3 + 3x3 = at most 13 calls; owner blanket approval, number fixed by session and recorded per stage

predictions.claim: Bare-vanilla canary lands in 14-60 with >=2 dimensions reported: a four-module underspecified orchestration rework breaks one-shot even under the partial-credit instrument.

predictions.falsified_if: gap <= 16 pts or reversed — the decisive win does NOT generalize to a second family and 0.6.2's claim gets scoped to the first family in the next manifest edit

predictions.claim: The loop iterates with progress on at least one trial (green at iteration >= 2, or shrinking failure fingerprints), as on the first family.
predictions.falsified_if: all oracle-loop trials green at iteration 1 (saturation for the loop arm) or all stall no-progress at the canary level (valid pins fail to force on this family)

predictions.claim: The multi-module axis shows up: vanilla-configured fixes the crash (params-contract family GREEN in >=2 of 3 trials — it is the loudest symptom) but leaves at least one cross-module behaviour family (resume-reuse or incremental-materialization) RED in a majority of trials; oracle-loop greens those under forcing.
predictions.falsified_if: vanilla-configured greens resume-reuse AND incremental-materialization in a majority of trials (the family is easier than designed), or oracle-loop cannot green them either (forcing fails on cross-module behaviours)

predictions.claim: Envelope: every oracle-loop trial ends with preserved-behaviour GREEN; no arm regresses the no-op paths.
